AcquisitionReport.description: Visits per day and channel, every channel named, the top sources and the top campaigns: the source is the campaign source, else the referring host, else "(direct)", and the campaign is utm_campaign, both taken from the first page view of the visit that carries a channel. Visits without a campaign are left out of campaigns.

BatchRequest.description: A batch of events from the browser, sent as text/plain or application/json. More than 50 events answer 413.

DevicesReport.description: Visits, conversion events and converting visits (both null without a conversion event) per value, sorted by visits: the top five values and "other" for the rest, unknown countries included.

EngagementReport.description: How the visits of the range entered, left and lasted: entry and exit pages, single-page visits and visit length, from the first to the last event of each visit.

entry_pages.description: The ten pages most visits started on

single_page_visits.description: Visits that started here and saw nothing else

exit_pages.description: The ten pages most visits ended on, by their last page view

median_visit_seconds.description: Median time from the first to the last event of a visit; null without visits

single_page_visits.description: Visits that viewed one page only

visit_lengths.description: The visits by length: under 10 s, 30 s, 1 min, 3 min, 10 min, 30 min, and more

up_to_seconds.description: Upper bound, exclusive, of the bucket; null for the last, open one

visits.description: Visits with a page view, the same count as the overview

ErasedSubject.description: How many events were deleted: the user's and those of every visit they identified in. Zero is success too, so a retry after a timeout is safe.

ErrorResponse.description: A stable machine key in error and a message for humans that never echoes input.

FeaturesReport.description: The 50 most used named events (kind=events) or screens by page views (kind=screens), with the visits they appear in and one daily count per day of the range.

FunnelReport.description: How many visits (mode=visit) or identified people (mode=user) reached each step, in order: a step counts only at or after the first time the previous one happened. median_seconds_from_previous is the median time, in whole seconds, between reaching the previous step and this one, among those who reached it (null on the first step or when nobody did); median_seconds_overall the same from the first step to the last.

FunnelSegmentsReport.description: The funnel per visit segment (visit mode only: a person has many devices): for each segment that reached the first step, the visits that reached each step, the largest segment first. The segments add up to the /funnel counts of the same steps.

segment.description: The device type of the visit, or the channel of its first attributed page view; "unknown" when the visit has none

steps.description: How many visits of the segment reached each step

FunnelSubjectsReport.description: The visits (mode=visit: session ids) or identified people (mode=user: user ids) behind one step of a funnel: outcome=reached those who reached step n (1 is the first), outcome=dropped those who reached step n - 1 and never step n. last_step_at is when they reached the last step they did; newest first, 50 per page. next_cursor goes back as cursor for the older page, null on the last one.

IncomingEvent.description: One event. An event that breaks these rules is counted as rejected while the rest of its batch is kept.

IngestResult.description: What happened to each event of the batch.

Me.description: The signed-in admin and the projects they may read.

first_event_at.description: When the oldest event kept for the project happened; null before the first

last_event_at.description: When the newest event of the project happened; null before the first

OverviewReport.description: Visits, identified users, conversions (null without a conversion event) and failed writes of the range against the previous one (the same number of days right before it), with one daily entry per day of each period.

comparison_cutoff.description: When the range ends today in the project time zone: the local time it was read at, and the previous period stops at that time on its last day. Null when the range is over and both periods are whole days.

converting_visits.description: Visits that sent the conversion event at least once; null without one

previous_days.description: One entry per day of the previous period, oldest first

ProjectSettings.description: The settings of a project, read-only: they change through the command line.

allowed_origins.description: The origins whose pages may send events with a public key

conversion_event.description: The event counted as a conversion; null when the project has none

event_retention_months.description: How many months an event is kept before the daily retention job deletes it

first_event_at.description: When the oldest event kept for the project happened; null before the first

last_event_at.description: When the newest event of the project happened; null before the first

public_keys.description: The live public keys, oldest first; a public key ships in the site, not a secret

secret_keys.description: The live secret keys, oldest first, by id and creation time only: a secret key is stored as a hash and never shown

timezone.description: The IANA time zone the days of every report are counted in

PropertyBreakdownReport.description: How the properties of one named event break down in the range. events counts the event; for each key, events counts those that carry it, values are its 10 most frequent values (text, as sent: true, 12.5) with their count and visits, and other_count the events with any other value. Keys come in order of the events that carry them; a reserved event (page_view, identify, api_request) answers 0 events and no keys.

RequestCodeRequest.description: The email to send a sign-in code to, and the language to write it in.

locale.description: The language of the dashboard asking, as a BCP 47 tag (en, pt-BR). The email is written in it when the API has it (matched on the language, so pt-PT gets pt-BR), else in English.

RequestsReport.description: Writes (methods other than GET, kind=writes) or failed reads (GET, kind=reads) per route, the most failing first: a failure is status 0 or 400 and above. Reads count failures only, so total equals failed and no rate can be drawn from them: a site may send a GET only when it fails. Screens are the pages the calls were made from; at most five recent failures per route, newest first. days counts the calls of every route per day by status class (success below 400, client_error 4xx, server_error 5xx, no_response status 0). route_days, only when a route is asked, gives that route per day: calls, failures, and the median and 95th percentile duration (null on a day without calls).

SignedIn.description: The signed-in admin; the session travels in a cookie.

SubjectEvents.description: Every event about the user, oldest first, 1,000 per page; pass next_after as after for the next page, null on the last one.

TimelineReport.description: The visits of a person (every visit with an event carrying the user id, the one they identified in included) or of one visit, newest first, 20 per page, with all their events. user_id is the first id the visit was identified with, null for an anonymous one. next_before is the cursor for the older page, null on the last one.

TimeOfDayReport.description: When the visits of the range started: for each weekday, Monday first, and each local hour, the visits whose first page view happened then. The grid adds up to the visits.

hours.description: Visits that started in each hour, 0 to 23, in the project time zone

weekday.description: ISO weekday: 1 is Monday, 7 is Sunday

VerifyCodeRequest.description: The email and the six-digit code it received.

VisitsReport.description: The visits with events in the range, newest first, 50 per page. A visit is one browser tab; nothing links two of them. entry_path is its first page view, highlights its first named events in order, failed_requests its api_request events with status 0 or 400 and above, source and campaign those of its entry page view (the source as Acquisition names it), user_id the id it was identified with. total counts every visit that matches the filters, on every page. next_cursor goes back as cursor for the older page, null on the last one.

secret_key.description: A secret project key: pyxis_sk_ followed by 32 letters and digits

info.description: Privacy-first product analytics: event ingestion, dashboard queries and erasure of a user's events. No cookies on tracked visitors, no personal data, no IP address or user agent stored.
info.title: Pyxis API

post.summary: Revoke the session and clear its cookie

post.description: Always answers 202: a code is created and emailed only when the email belongs to an admin.

200.description: Signed in; the session cookie is set.

post.summary: Exchange a sign-in code for a session cookie

options.summary: CORS preflight for the batch route

post.description: Public route, authenticated by the project key in the body and the Origin header. Invalid events are counted as rejected; the rest of the batch is stored. A resent event is a duplicate, never stored twice.

400.description: The body is not JSON or does not match BatchRequest.

401.description: The key is unknown or revoked.

403.description: The Origin header is missing or not one of the project's origins.

413.description: The body exceeds 32,768 bytes or holds more than 50 events.

429.description: Too many batches from this address or for this project.
